subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does repeated authenticated use of the bounded audit or ACP-history APIs create an in-scope availability vulnerability that requires endpoint-level throttling?
rationale: Source inspection does not support the reported recursive-filter primitive, but whether authenticated operator request volume needs an additional availability boundary depends on the project's security model and measured load behavior.

options.title: Request focused load proof
options.body: Keep the issue open while requesting a reproducible benchmark against the actual bounded RPC contract before changing security-sensitive query behavior.

options.title: Close as non-reproducible
options.body: Close after confirming that the fixed filter schema, result cap, authorization, and single-operator threat model adequately address the report.

options.title: Sponsor defense-in-depth throttling
options.body: Add endpoint-level throttling despite the missing reported primitive, with explicit limits and operator-impact tests.

recommendation.title: Request focused load proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while requesting a reproducible benchmark against the actual bounded RPC contract before changing security-sensitive query behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent ACP runtime work is the closest available ownership signal for confirming the actual request and replay boundary.
